contrast_basis: Anthropic supported binding frontier-model obligations, whereas the U.S. government code favors voluntary obligations.
OpenAI supported registration, disclosure, and licensing requirements, whereas the U.S. government code favors voluntary obligations.
Anthropic supported restrictions on certain model weights, whereas the U.S. government code is mixed on open-weight release.
Meta publicly advocated open model release before Llama 4, whereas the U.S. government code is mixed.
Both positions support chip export controls, but Anthropic explicitly argued that existing controls had not gone far enough.
Anthropic supported binding state requirements rather than waiting for federal consensus, whereas the U.S. government code favors reducing regulatory requirements.
